name: Noble Dollar

mechanismArchetypeReview.rationale: Noble documents USDN as a representation of M0's M token locked through the M0 Portal, with M0's Treasury-backed and rebasing design determining the underlying value. The direct USDN reserve relationship is therefore the M token, while the current individual Treasury allocations, fund claim terms, duration, NAV methodology, and loss-recovery design remain M0-level facts not disclosed by Noble's USDN documentation.

applicabilityBasis.summary: USDN is a rebasing yield-bearing stablecoin that accrues T-bill yield directly to holder balances every 30 seconds via M0's rebase mechanism. The GENIUS Act defines a payment stablecoin as one the issuer is obligated to redeem at a fixed monetary value; USDN balances grow over time rather than redeeming at a fixed amount. The Act also explicitly prohibits payment stablecoin issuers from paying any yield to holders — USDN's entire design is yield distribution. These structural features place USDN outside the GENIUS payment stablecoin definition.

genius.notes: USDN is a rebasing yield-bearing T-bill wrapper built on M0 infrastructure; it falls outside the GENIUS Act payment stablecoin definition because (1) it does not redeem at a fixed monetary value (balances rebase upward as yield accrues), and (2) its core design distributes yield directly to holders, which the Act prohibits for in-scope payment stablecoins. Noble's legal entity is NASD Inc (US-based); M0 provides infrastructure but is not the issuer. Noble announced migration from Cosmos appchain to EVM L1 in January 2026; USDN remains the flagship asset on the new chain.
